prompts:
Bug: `dateOrNull()` in C:\Aura\aura-roadmap\src\lib\domain\data.ts shifts every MariaDB DATE column back by one day in any positive-offset timezone (Europe/Bratislava is UTC+1/+2).

Cause: the mariadb pool in src/lib/db.ts does NOT set `dateStrings: true`, so a DATE column is returned as a JS `Date` at LOCAL midnight. `dateOrNull` goes through `isoOrNull` -> `toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, which converts to UTC first.

Proof (TZ=Europe/Bratislava):
 new Date(2026, 7, 10).toISOString().slice(0,10) -> "2026-08-09" // stored value was 2026-08-10

Affected call sites (all read real DATE columns):
- src/lib/domain/sprints.ts:306-307 startDate / endDate (sprints.start_date, sprints.end_date)
- src/lib/domain/workItems.ts:432 dueDate (work_items.due_date)
- src/lib/domain/worklogs.ts:57 workDate (worklogs.work_date)

Two possible fixes, pick one and apply it consistently:
1. Format in SQL: select DATE columns as `DATE_FORMAT(col, '%Y-%m-%d') AS col` and drop `dateOrNull` from those mappers. This is what src/lib/domain/checkpoints.ts and plans.ts already do (see the header note in checkpoints.ts) and it is driver-independent.
2. Rewrite `dateOrNull` to read LOCAL date fields (getFullYear/getMonth/getDate) when the value is a `Date`, instead of round-tripping through UTC. Keep `isoOrNull` as-is for DATETIME instants.

Add a unit test in src/lib/domain/data.test.ts that pins the behaviour with a `new Date(2026, 7, 10)` input (vitest already runs under TZ=Europe/Bratislava, so the test is a real guard). Also check whether any date is written back from these DTOs, which would compound the shift on each round trip.
